why: The heaviest bracing in the library, and the movements that curl the trunk against the abdominal wall. Both raise intra-abdominal pressure sharply — the load a hernia, a healing abdominal incision or an inflamed bowel is protected from.
movements: Ab Wheel Rollout; Barbell Deadlift; Barbell Hip Thrust; Barbell Romanian Deadlift; Barbell Squat; Cable Crunch; Crunches; Exercise Ball Crunch; Exercise Ball Pull-In; Front Barbell Squat; Good Morning; Hack Squat; Hanging Leg Raise; Hollow Body Hold; Leg Press; Leg Raise on Parallel Bars; Lying Leg Raise; Push Press; Rack Pull; Russian Twist; Sumo Deadlift
conditions_that_withhold_it: abdominal_surgery, diverticulitis, hemorrhoid, hernia, hiatal_hernia, ibd, inguinal_hernia, recent_surgery, ulcer, ulcerative_colitis

why: Balance on one leg, or a stepping movement, with load in the hands or on the back. A loss of balance here is a fall carrying weight — the risk for vertigo, neuropathy, Parkinson's, epilepsy, and for bone that fractures when it lands. Split squats with the back foot planted and machine work keep the same muscles without it.
movements: Barbell Lunge; Barbell Step Ups; Bulgarian Split Squat; Dumbbell Lunges; Dumbbell Step Ups; Reverse Lunge; Stair Climbing
conditions_that_withhold_it: bppv, epilepsy, labyrinthitis, multiple_sclerosis, neuropathy, osteoporosis, parkinson, seizure, stroke, vertigo, vestibular

why: Head below the heart. Inverted and decline positions raise intraocular and intracranial pressure, which is the mechanism glaucoma, retinopathy and a history of stroke are restricted for.
movements: Decline Push-Up; Hands-Elevated Pike Push-Up; Inchworm; Pike Push-Up; Pike Push-Up - Feet Elevated; Wall Handstand Hold
conditions_that_withhold_it: bppv, epilepsy, glaucoma, labyrinthitis, migraine, retinal_detachment, retinopathy, seizure, sinusitis, stroke, vertigo, vestibular

why: Load carried by or through the cervical spine: a bar resting on it, the traps shrugging a heavy load, a hand pulling the head forward. Restricted for cervical spondylosis, a neck injury and vertigo.
movements: Barbell Lunge; Barbell Shrug; Barbell Squat; Barbell Step Ups; Crunches; Dumbbell Shrug; Farmer's Walk; Good Morning; Wall Handstand Hold
conditions_that_withhold_it: bppv, cervical_disc, cervical_spondylosis, labyrinthitis, neck_injury, vertigo, vestibular, whiplash

why: A load that lands on the body if control is lost for a moment: a bar across the chest or the neck, a weight held over the face, a hang from a bar, a moving belt, open water. Machines and cables keep the load on a track, which is why they are the standard advice for epilepsy.
movements: Barbell Bench Press; Barbell Floor Press; Barbell Lunge; Barbell Shoulder Press; Barbell Squat; Barbell Step Ups; Chin-Up; Close-Grip Bench Press; Dumbbell Bench Press; Dumbbell Flyes; Dumbbell Overhead Triceps Extension - Two Hands; EZ-Bar Skullcrusher; Front Barbell Squat; Good Morning; Hanging Leg Raise; Incline Barbell Bench Press; Incline Dumbbell Press; Incline Treadmill Walk; Leg Raise on Parallel Bars; Lying Triceps Press; Pull-Up; Push Press; Stair Climbing; Swimming; Wall Handstand Hold

why: The lumbar spine taken toward end-range extension, or loaded there. Spondylolisthesis, spinal stenosis and facet pain are provoked by it. Herniated disc is deliberately not mapped here — extension is often the therapeutic direction for it — which is the yoga engine's reading too.
movements: Back Extension; Barbell Hip Thrust; Prone Swimmer; Push Press; Superman Hold; Wall Handstand Hold
conditions_that_withhold_it: compression_fracture, facet, osteoporosis, spinal_stenosis, spondylolisthesis, spondylolysis

why: Flexing, side-bending or twisting the trunk under load is the movement associated with vertebral compression fracture in low bone density. The spine is safest kept neutral while it is loaded; the anti-movement core work (dead bug, bird dog, Pallof press, planks) trains the same muscles without it.
movements: Cable Crunch; Crunches; Dumbbell Side Bend; Exercise Ball Crunch; Exercise Ball Pull-In; Good Morning; Hanging Leg Raise; Hollow Body Hold; Leg Raise on Parallel Bars; Lying Leg Raise; Russian Twist; Standing Cable Wood Chop

why: Bodyweight carried through an extended wrist. Rheumatoid and other inflammatory arthritis, carpal tunnel and a wrist injury are all aggravated by it; forearm planks and machine presses spare the joint.
